sections.h2: What makes selling a house in East Lansing different?
sections.html:
East Lansing is a college town built around Michigan State University, and its rental rules decide who can buy and use your house. The city requires a rental license for most non-owner-occupied homes, some neighborhoods bar new rentals, and many single-family houses carry deed restrictions against renting at all. Those facts change which buyers can pay full price.

The city sits in Ingham and Clinton counties, immediately east of Lansing. It was settled in 1847 and incorporated in 1907. The legislature approved a charter proposed under the name College Park but changed the name to East Lansing. MSU was founded in 1855 and moved onto what is now campus ground in 1857, and the city's first seven mayors were professors or college employees. East Lansing stayed a dry city until voters changed the charter in 1968.

Grand River Avenue, a boulevard that grew out of the old Lansing and Howell plank road, runs through downtown and separates the campus from the rest of the city together with Michigan Avenue.

sections.h2: How does East Lansing compare with nearby Michigan cities?
sections.html:
East Lansing has the highest median home value of the four cities in this group and the lowest share of owner-occupied homes. It is also young, with a median age of 21.8 at the 2020 census, so the housing stock turns over faster than in a suburb like Eastpointe.

Only about 59.5 percent of residents lived in the same house a year earlier, compared with 92.3 percent in Eastpointe. That turnover is why an East Lansing listing often meets buyers who plan to rent it out or buy as a first home near campus.

sections.h2: What rental rules affect the value of an East Lansing house?
sections.html:
If your buyer plans to rent the house, the license rules matter as much as the price. The city code lists exceptions where no license is needed, and a seller can help a buyer by knowing them.

  • Family of the owner may live in the house without a license, and two unrelated people count as a family.
  • An owner who is away temporarily may use a house-sitting form for up to two years in a five-year period, but a house that is for sale does not qualify.
  • A seller of a one- or two-family dwelling may stay up to 90 days after closing under a rental agreement without a license.
  • An estate representative may occupy a house for up to two years from the owner's date of death if the owner lived there for the last year.

Putting a house in an LLC removes the owner-occupancy exception, because an LLC has no family members. A new rental license is not automatic. Some areas have a zoning overlay that prohibits new licenses or limits them to owner-occupied homes, and the city's own guidance says a new application takes a minimum of two months and more often three to four. A tenant cannot move in before the license is granted.

sections.h2: Which neighborhoods, schools and roads do East Lansing buyers ask about?
sections.html:
The city lists more than 25 neighborhoods, and many have associations that speak at council and commission meetings. One section is a designated Historic District, and landmark structures in older areas fall under the Historic Preservation Code. Several single-family neighborhoods within a mile of campus have used a petition process under a 2004 zoning ordinance to restrict or prohibit renting.

East Lansing Public Schools covers most of the city, with six elementary schools, MacDonald Middle School and East Lansing High School, and just over 3,400 students. Portions of the city fall in the Lansing, Okemos, Haslett and Bath districts, so confirm the district on the deed address. About one fifth of the East Lansing district's students come from outside the city through Schools of Choice.

Interstates 96, 69 and 496 and US 127 serve the area, and CATA buses connect the city with Lansing. Amtrak runs the Blue Water service to Chicago from the Capital Area Multimodal Gateway on South Harrison Road. The Census puts mean commute time at 16.2 minutes, the shortest in this four-city group.

sections.h2: How do East Lansing property taxes work at closing?
sections.html:
The city treasury bills both seasons. Summer taxes are levied July 1 and payable without penalty through August 31. Winter taxes are levied December 1 and payable without penalty through February 14 of the following year. If a due date falls on a weekend or holiday, it moves to the next business day, and a 3 percent penalty applies after the due date.

On March 1 each year the city sends unpaid real property taxes to the county, with added interest and penalty. For a payoff after that date, call the Ingham County Treasurer at (517) 676-7220 or the Clinton County Treasurer at (989) 224-5280, depending on where the parcel sits. The city's property tax office is at 410 Abbot Road and can be reached at (517) 319-6826.

Because the city spans two counties, the register of deeds and the county treasurer that apply to you depend on the parcel. Ask the East Lansing assessor which county holds your records before you order a title commitment.

sections.h2: What state costs apply when an East Lansing house sells?
sections.html:
The seller owes the state transfer tax of $3.75 per $500 of value (MCL 207.525), plus a county amount of 55 cents per $500 where the county has fewer than 2,000,000 residents (MCL 207.504). Ask the register of deeds in your county to confirm the figure. The tax is due to the county treasurer within 15 days of delivering the deed.

MCL 207.526 exempts deeds to a child or grandchild, deeds in lieu of foreclosure and land contracts where title has not passed. After closing, the buyer reports the transfer to the assessor within 45 days, and the taxable value resets to the state equalized value the following year (MCL 211.27a). Ask the assessor how to rescind your principal residence exemption so the new owner's bill is correct.

sections.h2: What should an East Lansing owner compare before choosing a sale route?
sections.html: A listing aimed at students and landlords depends on the rental license history of the house, so gather license paperwork and any deed restriction notices first. An owner-occupant buyer cares about school district lines and neighborhood overlay rules instead. A direct sale to an investor can work for a house that needs repairs or has a lapsed license, as long as the contract states who handles the license process.

faqs.q: Do I need a rental license to sell my East Lansing house?
faqs.a: No. A license is a requirement for renting, not for selling. A seller of a one- or two-family dwelling may stay up to 90 days after closing under a rental agreement without a license, which can help when you need time to move.

faqs.q: Can an East Lansing buyer rent the house I am selling?
faqs.a: Maybe. Many single-family houses carry deed restrictions against renting, some neighborhoods have zoning overlays that bar new licenses, and a license application takes a minimum of two months. Buyers should call the city's Planning, Building and Housing department before closing.

faqs.q: When are East Lansing property taxes due?
faqs.a: Summer taxes are payable without penalty through August 31 and winter taxes through February 14. A 3 percent penalty applies afterward, and unpaid real property taxes go to the county on March 1.

faqs.q: Which county handles my East Lansing sale?
faqs.a: East Lansing lies in both Ingham and Clinton counties. Your parcel's records, deed recording and delinquent tax payoff go through whichever county holds it, so confirm with the city assessor before ordering title work.

faqs.q: Who pays the Michigan transfer tax?
faqs.a: The seller. The state rate is $3.75 per $500 of value, with a county rate added, and it is due to the county treasurer within 15 days after the deed is delivered. Deeds to a child or grandchild are exempt.
